about: Copeland is a climate technology company making compressors, controls and software for heating, cooling and refrigeration, including the Scroll and Copeland-brand compressors used in HVAC and cold chain systems. Sells to equipment makers and contractors worldwide. Headquartered in St Louis, Missouri (with operations in Sidney, Ohio); formerly Emerson's Climate Technologies, sold in 2023 to Blackstone in a deal that valued the business at about 14 billion dollars, with Emerson retaining a stake. B2B brand with low consumer awareness; the input's consumer electronics tag is inaccurate.

Foxconn Technology Group, formally Hon Hai Precision Industry, is the world's largest electronics contract manufacturer, assembling iPhones for Apple and servers, including for Nvidia AI, as well as electric vehicles through Foxtron and EV platforms. Revenue near 200 billion dollars and over 1 million employees, with plants in China, India, Vietnam, Mexico and the US. Headquartered in New Taipei City; founded 1974 by Terry Gou. Listed in Taipei (2317). B2B manufacturer, little consumer brand awareness.

South Korean maker of display panels, notably OLED and LCD screens for TVs, smartphones, monitors, laptops and cars, supplying LG Electronics, Apple, and automotive customers. Revenue near 20 trillion won. Headquartered in Seoul (Yeouido); established in 1985 as a joint venture, spun out in 1999 from LG. Listed on the Korea Exchange (034220) and New York (LPL), with LG Corp as the main shareholder. B2B component brand with limited consumer awareness.

AT&S is an Austrian maker of high-end printed circuit boards and IC substrates for smartphones, servers, AI chips and cars, with plants in Austria, China, India and Malaysia. Customers are major chip and electronics companies including Apple and Intel. Headquartered in Leoben, Styria; founded 1987. Listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (ATS). B2B component brand, essentially no consumer awareness; the consumer electronics tag in the input is a loose fit.

Columbus McKinnon designs and makes material handling equipment, such as hoists, cranes, chain, rigging and lifting products and intelligent motion control, serving industrial, entertainment, infrastructure and construction customers. Revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with historic roots in Amherst, New York; founded 1875. Listed on Nasdaq (CMCO). B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility, though its hoists are used in stage rigging.

VIAVI Solutions makes network test, measurement and assurance equipment and software for telecom carriers, data centers and cable operators, plus optical security and anti-counterfeiting coatings used on banknotes and in consumer electronics. Customers are network equipment makers, service providers and governments, with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Chandler, Arizona (formerly San Jose); spun out of JDS Uniphase in 2015. Listed on Nasdaq (VIAV). B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

Diodes Incorporated designs and supplies discrete, analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, including power management, protection and timing chips for automotive, industrial, computing, communications and consumer markets. Revenue near 1.3 billion dollars, with factories in Asia and the US. Headquartered in Plano, Texas; founded 1959. Listed on Nasdaq (DIOD). B2B component supplier with essentially no consumer awareness.

Texas Instruments is a leading analog and embedded processing semiconductor company, selling tens of thousands of chips and calculators (TI-84) to industrial, automotive, personal electronics and communications customers. Revenue near 16 billion dollars, with US wafer fabs in Texas, Utah and elsewhere. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas; founded 1930 as Geophysical Service. Listed on Nasdaq (TXN). B2B brand known to engineers and students, limited general consumer awareness.

Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing is, per Crunchbase, a semiconductor manufacturing company based in Koshi, Shimane, Japan, tagged under manufacturing and semiconductors. Total funding shown is about 747 billion yen, which suggests a very large chip fabrication project. The input does not give owners, products, customers or start date. B2B manufacturer. Limited public information - check before outreach.

about: AMETEK is a US manufacturer of electronic instruments and electromechanical devices, producing precision instrumentation, sensors, motors and aerospace components for aerospace, medical, industrial and power markets. Revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Berwyn, Pennsylvania; founded 1930. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (AME). B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Analog Devices designs analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing chips for industrial automation, automotive, communications, healthcare and consumer devices, after acquiring Maxim Integrated in 2021. Revenue near 10 billion dollars. Headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts; founded 1965. Listed on Nasdaq (ADI). B2B component brand, strong among engineers and automotive suppliers, with limited consumer visibility; it has sponsored Formula 1 teams.

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is a Chinese maker of DRAM memory chips for PCs, servers and phones, building production in Hefei, Anhui as part of China's drive for domestic chip supply. State-backed with local government funds and investors and funding of tens of billions of yuan. Headquartered in Hefei; founded 2016. It filed for an IPO on Shanghai's STAR market. B2B component maker with limited consumer awareness, subject to US export controls.

Emirates Global Aluminium is the largest industrial company in the UAE outside oil and gas and one of the largest aluminium producers in the world, with smelters in Abu Dhabi and Dubai and a US project in Oklahoma. Sells primary aluminium to manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, construction and packaging. Headquartered in Dubai; formed 2013 from Dubai Aluminium and Emirates Aluminium. Owned equally by Mubadala and the Investment Corporation of Dubai. B2B with low consumer visibility, but it has sports sponsorship links.

GlobalFoundries is a contract chipmaker producing semiconductors for automotive, IoT, aerospace and mobile, concentrating on specialty and mature nodes rather than leading-edge. Fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany, Singapore. Customers include AMD (original), Qualcomm and NXP, with revenue near 6.8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Malta (Saratoga County), New York; created 2009 from AMD. Listed on Nasdaq (GFS), majority owned by Mubadala. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Hubbell is a US maker of electrical and utility products, including grid infrastructure components, wiring devices, connectors and lighting for utilities, industrial, telecom and commercial customers. Revenue near 5.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut, founded 1888. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HUBB). B2B brand, with little consumer awareness.

IonQ is a US quantum computing company building trapped-ion systems and selling access through cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and direct contracts with enterprises and governments. Expanded through acquisitions including Oxford Ionics, Lightsynq and Capella. Headquartered in College Park, Maryland; founded 2015. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (IONQ). B2B technology company, with growing visibility among investors and little consumer awareness.

Jabil is a US electronics manufacturing services provider building products for others, including hardware for cloud and AI data centers, healthcare devices, automotive, communications and Apple components. Revenue near 29 billion dollars and around 140,000 employees in over 30 countries. Headquartered in St Petersburg, Florida; founded 1966. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (JBL). B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand profile.

Lumentum designs and makes optical and photonic components, including lasers for 3D sensing in smartphones, transceivers and optical networking components, and increasingly parts for AI data centers. Customers include Apple and cloud network equipment suppliers, with revenue near 1.5 to 2 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Jose, California; spun off from JDS Uniphase in 2015. Listed on Nasdaq (LITE). B2B component brand, with low consumer awareness.

Rapidus is a Japanese semiconductor foundry company founded in 2022 by Toyota, Sony, NTT, SoftBank, Denso, NEC, Kioxia and MUFG, aiming to produce 2-nanometer logic chips in Chitose, Hokkaido by 2027 with technology help from IBM. Backed heavily by Japanese government subsidies. Headquartered in Tokyo. Funding shown is around 726 billion yen. Pre-revenue B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness.

Semiconductor Manufacturing North China, Beijing-based per Crunchbase, is a chip foundry unit tied to China's SMIC, producing semiconductors for domestic customers. Funding shown is about 65 billion yuan. Input is limited, and detailed ownership and product lines are not confirmed here. B2B manufacturer with no consumer awareness. Limited public information - check before outreach.

about: Solstice Advanced Materials is a US specialty materials company spun out of Honeywell in October 2025, making refrigerants (Solstice low-global-warming products), electronic materials, nuclear and medical packaging materials and fluorine chemicals. Customers are industrial and electronics manufacturers. Headquartered in Morris Plains, New Jersey. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (SOLS). B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

TeamSystem is Italy's largest provider of management software, offering cloud accounting, payroll, e-invoicing and ERP software to small and mid-size businesses and accountants in Italy, Spain, Germany and France. Headquartered in Pesaro, Italy; founded 1979. Owned by private equity firm Hellman & Friedman (majority investment from 2022). B2B brand with reasonable awareness among Italian accountants.

about: Wesco International is a business-to-business distributor of electrical, industrial and communications products and supply chain services, serving utilities, data centers, construction and industrial customers in the US, Canada and beyond. Revenue near 22 billion dollars. Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; roots to 1922 as Westinghouse Electric Supply. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (WCC) and acquired Anixter in 2020. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Grover is a German consumer electronics rental company offering subscriptions to phones, laptops, wearables, cameras and appliances for flexible months. Headquartered in Berlin; founded 2015. Customers are consumers and businesses in Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Spain and the US. Raised significant venture and debt funding, shown at around 2.3 billion dollars, including large debt facilities. Private. Well-known among young European consumers with strong digital marketing.

UNISOC is a Chinese fabless chip designer making mobile processors (including 4G and 5G smartphone chips), IoT and TV chips, formerly Spreadtrum and RDA, and sells to phone makers such as Samsung, Transsion and Realme. Headquartered in Shanghai. Backed by Tsinghua Unigroup, and later by state funds and Chinese investors. Funding shown is about 2.1 billion dollars. B2B chip supplier with minimal consumer awareness.

Ceconomy is the German parent of consumer electronics retailers MediaMarkt and Saturn, which run hundreds of stores in Europe, with an online and services business. Revenue near 23 billion euros. Headquartered in Dusseldorf; separated from Metro in 2017. Listed in Frankfurt (CEC). China's JD.com agreed in 2025 to acquire Ceconomy for roughly 2.2 billion euros. MediaMarkt and Saturn are well-known consumer brands across Europe with a history of football and sports sponsorship.

Hawaiian Electric Industries is the Hawaii holding company for Hawaiian Electric, the state's electric utility serving most of its population, and American Savings Bank (sold stake in 2025 plan). Earns regulated utility revenue of roughly 3.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Honolulu. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HE). The utility faced major legal liabilities after the August 2023 Maui wildfires. Known locally in Hawaii, with a regulated service and no wider consumer reach.

Videotron is a Quebec-based telecommunications and media company, owned by Quebecor, offering mobile, internet, television and cable services, with Freedom Mobile acquired in 2023 expanding it nationally. Customers are consumers and businesses mostly in Quebec, with the new Freedom mobile brand elsewhere in Canada. Headquartered in Montreal. Parent Quebecor is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (QBR.B). Funding shown is about 1.5 billion Canadian dollars. Strong consumer brand in Quebec.

Lowe's is the second-largest US home improvement retailer, headquartered in Mooresville, North Carolina. It operates about 1,700 stores in the US and Canada selling appliances, tools, building materials, hardware, lawn and garden products and home decor, to homeowners, DIY customers and professional contractors, online and in store. Annual revenue is around $80-85bn with roughly 300,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (LOW). Very high consumer brand visibility in North America and a long-time major sports sponsor, notably NASCAR, where it has been a headline sponsor of Hendrick Motorsports.

Micron Technology is a Boise, Idaho semiconductor maker, one of the three largest producers of DRAM memory and a major NAND flash maker. It sells memory and storage chips to data centers, AI server makers, smartphone, PC, automotive and industrial customers, and sells consumer SSDs and memory under the Crucial brand. Revenue is $25bn+ with around 48,000 employees and fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan, Singapore and elsewhere. Listed on the Nasdaq (MU). Mostly a B2B brand, with Crucial giving some consumer and gamer awareness.

Nidec Corporation is a Kyoto-headquartered Japanese maker of electric motors, one of the world's largest. It produces precision small motors for hard drives, appliances and cars, plus automotive traction motors, e-axles, robotics, industrial and appliance motors and machine tools, with revenue of roughly JPY 2.3 trillion and over 100,000 staff across more than 40 countries. Customers are automakers, electronics firms and industrial companies. Listed in Tokyo (6594) and on the NYSE until delisting there. Largely B2B, well known in industry but little consumer visibility.

Electrolux is a Stockholm-based Swedish appliance maker, selling refrigerators, ovens, washing machines, dishwashers, vacuum cleaners and air purifiers under Electrolux, AEG, Frigidaire and Westinghouse brands to consumers across Europe, North and Latin America, Asia and Australia. Revenue is about SEK 130bn and it employs around 45,000 people, with manufacturing in many countries. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ELUX B). Large household-name brand with strong visibility in Europe, and active in sports and F1-adjacent sponsorships in some markets.

Command Alkon is a Hilliard, Ohio software company serving the heavy building materials industry, supplying dispatch, ticketing, ordering and logistics software for ready-mixed concrete, aggregates and asphalt producers worldwide. Its customers are material producers and contractors, paid through software subscriptions and licences. Majority-owned by private equity firm Thoma Bravo, which acquired it in 2021 (originally from Francisco Partners). Private. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

indie Semiconductor is an Aliso Viejo, California fabless chip company focused on automotive electronics, selling chips and modules for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), LiDAR, radar, in-cabin sensing, connectivity and electrification. Customers are automakers and Tier-1 suppliers such as Aptiv, Bosch and Continental. It listed on the Nasdaq (INDI) via a 2021 SPAC merger and has acquired companies including Symeo and GEO Semiconductor. B2B component supplier, with no consumer profile.

Innoviz Technologies is an Israeli automotive LiDAR maker, with US operations noted in Santa Clara, California, whose InnovizOne and InnovizTwo sensors and perception software help vehicles see the road for autonomous driving and ADAS. Customers include automakers like BMW, Volkswagen group firm CARIAD, Mobileye (a distribution partner) and Mobileye-linked partners. Listed on Nasdaq (INVZ) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Collective Growth. B2B automotive technology supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

SemiDrive is a Nanjing-based Chinese fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2018, specialising in automotive chips for smart cockpits, ADAS, central computing and vehicle control, covering the X9, V9, G9 and E3 families. Customers include Chinese automakers and Tier-1 suppliers, and it has shipped millions of chips with funding of around $650m from investors such as Hillhouse and Qualcomm Ventures. Private, with a Hong Kong IPO expected. B2B, without consumer brand awareness.

Fab 34 JV is Intel's semiconductor manufacturing joint venture in Leixlip, County Kildare, Ireland, where Intel 4 and Intel 3 process chips are made in a large fab. In 2024 Apollo Global Management agreed to buy a 49% stake in the venture for about $11bn, funding Intel's expansion. The business is a fabrication facility with no consumer brand of its own. B2B chip production, no consumer awareness, and poor sponsorship fit.

about: MediaTek is a Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company based in Hsinchu, designing system-on-chips for smartphones (Dimensity), tablets, smart TVs, Wi-Fi routers, IoT devices, Chromebooks and cars. It sells to phone and electronics makers including Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo and Samsung, and is the largest smartphone chip supplier by volume. Annual revenue is about NT$ 530bn, with over 20,000 employees. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2454). Mostly B2B, though its logo appears on devices and it has sponsored sport and F1-adjacent campaigns.

Amkor Technology is one of the largest outsourced semiconductor packaging and test providers, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. It assembles and tests chips for fabless firms and chipmakers such as Apple, Qualcomm and Nvidia, with plants in South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, China, Vietnam, Malaysia and Portugal, plus an Arizona advanced packaging site under construction. Revenue is about $6-7bn. Listed on Nasdaq (AMKR), with the founding Kim family a major shareholder. B2B manufacturing, no consumer brand awareness.

Amprion is a German electricity transmission system operator based in Dortmund, running the extra-high-voltage grid across western and southwestern Germany, around 11,000 km of lines serving roughly 29 million people. It earns regulated grid fees and is building major HVDC corridors such as A-Nord and Ultranet. Owned by a consortium of German financial investors and Mercator-linked institutions, with RWE holding a minority stake. Private. Infrastructure utility with very low consumer visibility.

ams OSRAM is an Austrian-German photonics and sensor company formed when ams AG acquired OSRAM in 2020, based in Premstaetten, Austria with Munich operations. It makes LEDs, lasers, optical sensors and microsensors used in smartphones, cars (headlights, interior lighting), industrial and medical devices. Customers include automakers, Apple and other electronics firms. Revenue is about EUR 3.4bn with roughly 20,000 employees. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (AMS). B2B component maker, though the Osram name is known to consumers from lighting.

Applied Optoelectronics is a Sugar Land, Texas maker of optical communications chips, lasers and transceivers for data centers, cable TV broadband, telecom and FTTH networks. Customers include hyperscale cloud operators such as Amazon and Microsoft, and cable companies, with manufacturing in Texas, Taiwan and China. Listed on Nasdaq (AAOI), founded in 1997. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars a year. B2B components supplier, no consumer awareness.

Asus Global is the Singapore-based regional subsidiary of ASUSTeK Computer, the Taiwanese maker of laptops, desktops, motherboards, graphics cards, monitors, phones and gaming brand Republic of Gamers (ROG). Asus sells through retailers and online worldwide, with group revenue above $15bn. The parent is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2357). The input shows funding of about $2bn, likely an internal or financing figure. Very strong consumer and gamer brand, and ASUS has sponsored motorsport and esports in several markets.

about: Emerson is a St. Louis, Missouri automation technology company supplying control systems, valves, measurement instruments, test and measurement tools (NI) and industrial software to process, hybrid and discrete manufacturers. Customers include oil and gas, chemical, power, life science and semiconductor firms in over 150 countries, with revenue near $17-18bn. Listed on the NYSE (EMR), and took full ownership of AspenTech in 2025. Mostly B2B, a long-standing engineering brand with little consumer visibility.

Fortive is a Everett, Washington industrial technology company, spun out of Danaher in 2016, whose operating units include Fluke (test equipment), Tektronix, Gordian, Accruent and Provation, Ralliant spun off in 2025. Customers are engineers, contractors, utilities and healthcare firms worldwide, with revenue near $4bn. Listed on the NYSE (FTV). Largely B2B, though Fluke is well known to technicians; no consumer brand beyond that.

Forward Industries is a design, sourcing and manufacturing company for carry cases and protective solutions, historically for medical devices (diabetic kits), tools and consumer electronics, under its Forward Industries Design Group. In 2025 it pivoted to a Solana digital asset treasury strategy, with a large private placement led by Galaxy Digital, Jump Crypto and Multicoin. Listed on Nasdaq (FORD), with the HQ shown as Austin, Texas. Small B2B supplier turned crypto treasury vehicle, with no consumer awareness.

ITC Holdings is a Novi, Michigan electricity transmission company, the largest independent transmission operator in the US, with around 17,000 circuit miles of high-voltage lines across Michigan, Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois, Missouri, Kansas and Oklahoma. It earns regulated returns on grid investment. Owned by Fortis Inc. of Canada since 2016, with minority stakes sold to investors such as GIC and CPP Investments. B2B regulated utility with no consumer brand profile.

PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California quantum computing company building a fault-tolerant, utility-scale photonic quantum computer with silicon photonics chips manufactured with GlobalFoundries. It is constructing sites in Brisbane, Australia and Chicago, backed by government funding. It raised $1bn in 2025 at a valuation of $7bn from BlackRock, Temasek and Baillie Gifford, with total funding above $2.5bn. Private. Prominent in deep-tech, with no consumer products.

Silicon Box is a Singapore-based advanced semiconductor packaging company, founded in 2021, which builds chiplet integration and panel-level packaging for AI, high-performance computing and mobile customers. It runs a foundry in Singapore with a plant in Novara, Italy under development, backed by an EU-supported investment of EUR 3.2bn. Investors include Temasek and Sequoia. Private. B2B manufacturer, with no consumer visibility.

SiTime is a Santa Clara, California fabless chip company making MEMS-based silicon timing devices, including oscillators and clock generators, which replace quartz crystals in data centers, AI servers, automotive, industrial and mobile products. Customers are electronics and telecom equipment makers. Listed on Nasdaq (SITM), it was founded in 2003 and was held by MegaChips before its 2019 IPO. B2B component supplier, no consumer awareness.

TTM Technologies is a Santa Ana, California manufacturer of printed circuit boards, RF components and assemblies serving aerospace and defence, data center and networking, automotive and medical customers, with plants in North America and Asia. Revenue is about $2.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TTMI). B2B supplier with no consumer awareness.

Tsinghua Unigroup was a Chinese state-backed semiconductor and technology conglomerate, with a base in Beijing, owned by Tsinghua Holdings, which includes memory-chip firm YMTC, mobile chip designer Unisoc and server group H3C. It defaulted on bonds in 2020 and went through a bankruptcy restructuring in 2021-22 and was bought by a consortium led by Wise Road Capital and Jianguang Asset Management. A B2B chip group with big strategic importance in China and no consumer brand.

OSRAM is the Munich-based lighting and semiconductor company, long a household name for light bulbs and automotive lighting, which became part of ams OSRAM in 2020 when Austria's ams AG acquired it for about EUR 4.6bn. It makes LEDs, lasers, sensors and automotive lamps (Osram and Sylvania brands). Customers are carmakers, electronics firms and consumers. Part of ams OSRAM (SIX: AMS). Well-known consumer lighting brand, especially in Germany.

Repay (REPAY Holdings) is an Atlanta, Georgia electronic payment processing company providing integrated card and ACH processing, merchant acquiring and bill-pay software to businesses in niche verticals such as auto lending, consumer finance and healthcare. Revenue is near $300m. Listed on Nasdaq (RPAY) since a 2019 SPAC combination with Thunder Bridge. B2B fintech, with no consumer brand awareness. Crunchbase lists the country as Georgia (the US state).

United Nova Technology is described by Crunchbase as a company providing system manufacturing in electronics for the automotive industry, based in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, China. The input lists automotive and electronics industries and funding of about CNY 5.3bn with the latest round in September 2025. Products, customers and ownership are not stated. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Applied Materials is a Santa Clara, California supplier of semiconductor and display manufacturing equipment, including deposition, etch, ion implant and inspection tools, plus services, serving chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung and Intel. Revenue is near $28bn with about 35,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (AMAT). B2B equipment maker, one of the world's largest in its field, with little consumer awareness.

KnowBe4 is a Clearwater, Florida security awareness training and simulated phishing platform used by over 70,000 organisations to train employees. Vista Equity Partners took it private in 2023 for about $4.6bn, and it later acquired Egress and was folded into the KnowBe4 and Egress offering. Revenue was near $350m before the buyout. Private. B2B cybersecurity brand with high awareness among IT teams but little consumer awareness.

Legrand is a French maker of electrical and digital building infrastructure, based near Limoges and managed from Croissy-Beaubourg, producing switches, sockets, cable management, data center power and connected home products under brands such as Legrand, Bticino and Arnould. Revenue is about EUR 8.5bn with over 38,000 employees, selling in nearly 90 countries. Listed on Euronext Paris (LR). B2B and installer-focused, but switches and sockets are in most European homes; modest consumer brand awareness.

OSI Systems is a Hawthorne, California designer and maker of security screening systems (Rapiscan), healthcare patient monitoring (Spacelabs) and optoelectronic devices, with products sold to airports, customs agencies, hospitals and electronics firms in over 100 countries. Revenue is near $1.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (OSIS). B2B and government supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Progress Software is a Burlington, Massachusetts enterprise software company selling application development, data integration, content management and cybersecurity tools, such as Telerik, Sitefinity, MarkLogic, MOVEit and ShareFile, to developers and businesses. Revenue is around $950m. Listed on Nasdaq (PRGS). B2B software with recognition among developers, and little consumer awareness.

Grupo Energia Bogota is a Colombian multinational energy group based in Bogota, active in electricity transmission, natural gas transportation and distribution (including the Cálidda network in Peru) and power generation in Colombia, Peru, Brazil and Guatemala. Customers are utilities, industrial users and households through regulated tariffs. Majority-owned by the Bogota city government and listed on the Colombian stock exchange (GEB). Roughly a century old and a regional infrastructure leader. B2B and regulated utility, low consumer brand awareness outside Colombia.

Alliance Laundry Systems is a Ripon, Wisconsin manufacturer of commercial laundry equipment, selling washers and dryers under the Speed Queen, UniMac, Huebsch, IPSO and Primus brands. Customers are laundromats, multi-housing laundry operators, hotels, and institutions, plus Speed Queen home laundry sold to consumers. Revenue runs in the billions of dollars with global distribution. Long owned by private equity (BDT Capital and others); it completed a US IPO in 2025 (NYSE: ALH). Speed Queen has solid consumer recognition in North America; mostly B2B overall.

GoPro is a San Mateo, California maker of action cameras (HERO series, MAX 360), mounts and accessories, plus a subscription service for cloud storage and editing. Founded in 2002 by Nick Woodman, it sells through retailers and online to consumers, adventure athletes and creators in about 100 countries. Listed on Nasdaq (GPRO) since 2014; revenue has fallen from a peak above $1.5 billion. Strong consumer brand in action sports and has a history of sports sponsorship.

Advanced Energy Industries is a Denver, Colorado-based maker of precision power conversion and control systems (Fort Collins origins) for semiconductor equipment, industrial thin-film, data center, telecom and medical applications. Founded in 1981, listed on Nasdaq (AEIS), with roughly $1.5 billion annual revenue. Customers are equipment manufacturers such as Applied Materials and Lam Research. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Cloover is a Berlin-based energy-transition fintech providing embedded financial services and software for solar, storage and heat-pump installers. It offers financing, a sales platform and project management software, enabling installers to sell energy systems to households. Founded around 2021 and has raised about $1.4 billion mostly as debt facilities, with offices in Germany and elsewhere in Europe. B2B, with limited public brand awareness.

about: ContourGlobal is a London-headquartered power generation company, founded in 2005, that owns and operates thermal, hydro, wind and solar plants across Europe, Latin America, Africa and the US. It sells electricity mainly under long-term contracts to utilities and grids, and has been growing its clean energy share. KKR acquired it in 2022 and took it private from the London stock market. B2B energy, with little consumer brand awareness.

about: Koch, Inc. is a privately held US conglomerate based in Wichita, Kansas, owned by the Koch family. Its businesses include Koch Industries, Flint Hills Resources, Georgia-Pacific, Molex, INVISTA, Koch Fertilizer and Koch Engineered Solutions, spanning refining, chemicals, paper products, electronics, agriculture and ranching. Revenue exceeds $100 billion with about 120,000 employees in over 60 countries. Consumer brands include Brawny, Dixie and Angel Soft. Private ownership. High brand exposure via consumer paper goods.

Semtech is a Camarillo, California supplier of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, including LoRa wireless chips for IoT, signal integrity products for data centers, and protection devices, sold to electronics makers in data center, industrial and consumer markets. Founded in 1960, listed on Nasdaq (SMTC), with annual revenue around $900 million. Customers are OEMs, not end consumers. B2B component supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Trench Group is a Germany-based maker of high-voltage electrical equipment such as instrument transformers, bushings and air-core reactors for utilities and industry. It was carved out from Siemens Energy in 2024 and is owned by Triton, the private equity firm, with a significant investment of about 1.4 billion. Operates plants in Germany, Canada, the US, Brazil and elsewhere. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Its industries are electronics and manufacturing, and reported funding is about HK$7.16 billion. Beyond this, the input does not support any statement on products, customers or owners. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Huahong Group is a Shanghai-based Chinese state-owned semiconductor group, parent of Hua Hong Semiconductor, which operates specialty chip foundries (200mm and 300mm) producing embedded non-volatile memory, power and analog chips for automotive, industrial and consumer electronics customers. Hua Hong Semiconductor is listed in Hong Kong (1347) and Shanghai (688347). State-owned. B2B supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

NextNav is a McLean, Virginia-based company that operates a terrestrial positioning network providing 3D location, including floor-level altitude, and resilient GPS-alternative timing and navigation using licensed spectrum. Customers are wireless carriers, government and public safety agencies. Listed on Nasdaq (NN) since 2021, with reported funding of about $913 million. B2B technology with very limited consumer brand awareness.

Tata Electronics is the electronics manufacturing arm of the Tata Group, based in India, making precision components and assembling products such as Apple iPhones (acquired Wistron and Pegatron's Indian operations), and building a semiconductor fab in Dholera and an OSAT plant in Assam. Customers are global electronics brands. A Tata Sons subsidiary with major investments of over 100 billion rupees reported. B2B manufacturing; the Tata name has very high awareness in India.

Mirion Technologies is an Atlanta, Georgia-based provider of radiation detection, measurement, analysis and monitoring products for nuclear power plants, defense, healthcare (radiation therapy QA) and laboratories. Listed on NYSE (MIR) after a 2021 SPAC merger with GS Acquisition Holdings II, with annual revenue near $900 million. Customers are utilities, hospitals, governments and labs. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Sony Group is a Tokyo-based Japanese conglomerate, founded in 1946, with segments in games and network services (PlayStation), music (Sony Music), pictures (Sony Pictures), electronics (Bravia TVs, Alpha cameras, Xperia phones, headphones), imaging and sensors, and financial services.
